newsitem.title: USA: Optical Sensors sets holder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Optical Sensors sets holder rights plan.

text.p: Optical Sensors Inc said Wednesday that it adopted a shareholder rights plan aimed at protecting the company and its holders from unsolicited attempts or inequitable offers to acquire it.
The rights plan has no immediate dilutive effect and does not hurt the company's ability to accept a fair offer, it added.

"The rights agreement was not adopted in response to any specific effort to acquire control of the company and the directors of Optical Sensors are not aware of any such effort," Sam Humphries, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Under the rights plan, the company declared a dividend distribution of one preferred share purchase right for each common share outstanding as of January 8, 1997. Each right would enable shareholders to buy one one-thousandth of a share of series A junior preferred stock at an exercise price of $90.

The rights would be exercisable 10 days after a person or group acquired 15 percent or more of the company's common stock, a person or group began a tender offer to acquire 15 percent or more of the stock, or the company's directors determined that an "adverse person" was attempting to acquire control.
The company will be entitled to redeem the rights at $0.001 each at certain times. The rights expire on December 2, 2006. The plan also includes other provisions.
Optical Sensors markets an arterial blood gas monitoring system.
